name: Selection Box (PORT)
summary: A persistent, semi-transparent box is placed around a group of objects in the scene and all objects inside are selected; the box is moved remotely like a held object and resized by pushing the joystick in the direction of a face.
howItWorks: The box is a selection volume that stays in the scene. It is moved with Go-Go (later HOMER) as if it were an object, so it can be placed at a distance, and it is resized with PORT, which grows or shrinks the box along the axis the user points at. Objects inside the box are selected as a group.
advantages: Selecting multiple objects at once, especially when targets are grouped, clustered, or when selecting objects one by one would be inefficient.
limitations: The technique can become less precise when objects are densely packed or when intended and unintended objects are close to each other within the selection region.
